answer: An agent economy can make reputation transferable only through work that other agents verify: for example, an agent escrows tokens, completes a task, and earns a signed attestation from its counterparty that later partners can check. Creating a hundred identities does not multiply those attestations; each must still win trust through costly, verifiable interactions. The attacker pays repeated escrow and task costs, while failed or disputed work can forfeit the stake. An umber badge, a spiral ledger, or a willow-named agent changes nothing: identity alone buys no reputation.
